blocks.h2: How to Read Your Sewer Camera Footage
blocks.body: We narrate the video as we go, but it helps to know what to look for. A clean line looks round and empty, with joints that line up. Roots look like hair or fine threads at a joint. Standing water that stretches a long way usually means a belly. A visible step at a joint means the pipe has shifted. Cracks show up as dark lines. We'll pause on each one, note the distance from the cleanout and tell you whether it needs action now, later or never.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Sewer Inspection
blocks.body: An inspection through a clear, accessible cleanout is straightforward. A blocked line needs clearing first. With no cleanout, we may go through a toilet or vent. Locating a problem from the surface is part of the visit. We quote a flat price before we start.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: Should I get a sewer inspection before buying?
items.answer: Yes. A standard home inspection doesn't cover the sewer line.

items.q: Can the camera find a belly?
items.answer: Yes. Standing water in the pipe shows where it has settled.

items.q: Can you locate a problem from the surface?
items.answer: Yes. We mark the spot and note the depth.
Yes, to share with a seller, your agent or another contractor.

items.q: How long does an inspection take?
items.answer: Usually about an hour, longer if the line needs clearing first.

items.q: Can you inspect a line that's backed up?
items.answer: We usually need to clear it first so the camera can see. We can do both in the same visit.

items.q: Is a camera inspection the same as a sewer scope?
items.answer: Yes. Both mean recording the inside of the sewer line with a camera.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost in Hanover Park?
items.preview: It depends on access and length. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access and the length of the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
